title: 1962 AHSME Problem 24
statement: Three machines \(P,\) \(Q,\) and \(R,\) working together, can do a job in \(x\) hours. When working alone, \(P\) needs an additional \(6\) hours to do the job; \(Q,\) one additional hour; and \(R,\) \(x\) additional hours. The value of \(x\) is:

solutions.text:
The rates satisfy \[ \frac1{x+6}+\frac1{x+1}+\frac1{2x}=\frac1x. \] Thus \[ \frac1{x+6}+\frac1{x+1}=\frac1{2x}, \] which simplifies to \(3x^2+7x-6=0,\) or \((3x-2)(x+3)=0.\) A time must be positive, so \(x=\frac{2}{3}.\)

Therefore, the correct answer is A.
hints: The individual completion times are \(x+6,\) \(x+1,\) and \(2x\)
Set the sum of the individual hourly rates equal to \(\frac{1}{x}\)
